segments.t: While Chef Barinov begs through the door for his phone, Kristina corners Max in the dining room and makes it clear she always gets what she wants in her own restaurant. When Max says she can fire him, she threatens to fire Kostya instead unless Max comes to her after work.
Пока вы будете ко мне приставать.
Максим, я всегда добиваюсь того, чего хочу.
Не могла бы ты мне дать свой?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'At least give me back my phone!' Notice how Russian expresses 'phone' and 'give' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Nastya answers right away.
Пока вы будете ко мне приставать.
'As long as you keep hitting on me.' In Russian, the idea of 'for now' flows naturally into 'to pester' without extra filler words.
Максим, я всегда добиваюсь того, чего хочу.
'Maksim, I always get what I want.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Maxim' before landing on 'want'.
'Especially in my own restaurant.' The grammar packs 'that' and 'restaurant' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Nastya answers right away.
'But you do not own the people.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'but' and finishing on 'people'.
'You can even fire me if you want.' Kristina brings out the contrast between 'can' and 'me' in a few short words.
'Why fire you?' Max raises the pitch on 'you' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Nastya answers right away.
'Well, or fire your friend Kostya.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'guest' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'And here is why.' Kristina anchors the line on 'and', while 'what' completes the thought.
'I am waiting for you after work.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'of work' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Nastya answers right away.
'Here is the thing.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'here' before landing on 'matter'.
Не могла бы ты мне дать свой?
'Could you possibly give me yours?' Kristina addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'his own'.
'Not a chance.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'what'. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Пока вы будете ко мне приставать.
Максим, я всегда добиваюсь того, чего хочу.
Не могла бы ты мне дать свой?

That wraps up this scene as in the dining room, Kristina corners Max and threatens to fire him or his friend Kostya over a broken bottle of vintage wine unless Max meets her after work. See you next time!
